title: These Galápagos Sea Turtles Didn't Wander — They Stayed Home
summary: Sea turtles are the long-distance champions of the ocean. They can sense Earth's magnetic field, the sun, and currents to travel thousands of kilometers. So when scientists tagged nine green sea turtles in the Galápagos, they expected the turtles to eventually swim far away to nest. Instead, the turtles stayed close to home. The team attached satellite transmitters to seven males and two females in 2015. They gave the turtles nicknames like Bernardo, Sara, Leandro, and Ainoa. Over three years, none of the turtles left the Galápagos Marine Reserve — a protected area of about 198,000 square kilometers. Most stayed near shallow coastal waters. Five of the nine barely left a single island. Ainoa was the most adventurous: she traveled from San Cristóbal to Santa Cruz and then to Isabela. The turtles only moved between islands during the cooler months, from April to October. On average, each turtle used a home range of about 1,498 square kilometers. That's still a big area, but nothing compared to the ocean-crossing trips sea turtles are known for. The researchers say this doesn't mean the turtles never migrate — they only tracked them for a limited time. But it does show that some turtles are far more homebound than anyone expected. The Galápagos is the only place where two genetically distinct forms of green sea turtles — yellow morphs and black morphs — share the same waters. Learning how yellow morphs use the reserve could help protect them.
why_it_matters: It shows that animals don't always behave the way we predict, and that protecting a big area of ocean can matter just as much as protecting a single beach.

background_read: The Galápagos (a group of volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean, about 1,000 kilometers west of Ecuador) are famous for animals found nowhere else, like giant tortoises and marine iguanas.
In 1835, the scientist Charles Darwin visited the Galápagos, and the unusual animals he saw there helped him build his ideas about how species change over time.
Green sea turtles are long-lived animals — they can swim for many decades and often come back to the very beach where they hatched to lay their own eggs.
Article_Structure: WHO: Nine green sea turtles with nicknames like Bernardo, Sara, Leandro and Ainoa, plus the scientists who tagged them with satellite transmitters.
WHAT: The turtles stayed close to home instead of swimming thousands of kilometers away to nest.
WHERE: The Galápagos Marine Reserve, around islands such as San Cristóbal, Santa Cruz and Isabela.
WHY: Learning how yellow morphs use the reserve could help protect them.

perspectives.description: They are happy because knowing exactly where the turtles swim can help people decide which parts of the ocean to protect.
They warn that the team only tracked the turtles for a limited time, so we cannot say turtles never migrate.
The turtles were tagged in 2015 and stayed put for three years — interesting, but one small group of animals doesn't speak for all sea turtles.
